chief_complaint: Fever, joint pain, headache, and nausea over the past 5 days.
history_of_present_illness: He has a history of cerebral infarction without neurological sequelae, hypertension and ulcerative colitis, and is taking antiplatelet, antihypertensive medicine, and subcutaneous injection of the TNF-alpha Blocker adalimumab once every 2 weeks.
exposure_and_epidemiology: He lives in a suburb of a city in Kyushu district, southwestern Japan, and has opportunities to encounter wild animals such as boars and deer; he has no recent history of overseas travel.
vitals: Body temperature 37 0C (98.6 0F), pulse rate 101 bpm, blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, SpO2 96% with 71 oxygen, and respiratory rate 32 breaths per minute.
physical_exam: The patient looked unwell and drowsy, had a normal chest examination, Glasgow Coma Scale 13/15 (E3V4M6), livedo reticularis bilaterally on lower extremities, no rash, and an enlarged left inguinal lymph node.
labs_and_diagnostics: Laboratory results showed elevated AST/ALT, LDH, CK, and low platelets, with the diagnosis of SFTS confirmed by detecting SFTS virus in blood serum by real-time RT-PCR, which is 98.6% sensitive and 99.1% specific.
differential_diagnosis: Acute fever with respiratory distress and impaired consciousness suggested sepsis, with pneumonia, meningitis, infective endocarditis, and tick- and mite-borne infectious diseases (Japanese spotted fever, scrub typhus, and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome) included in the differential diagnosis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was intubated and admitted to ICU, received meropenem and vancomycin (later discontinued), symptomatic and supportive treatment including fluid administration, noradrenaline, and hydrocortisone for non-responsive septic shock, showed gradual improvement, and was discharged on day 35 without sequelae.
